issue: Single-rule recall items are labeled skill "analysis" and difficulty 3 (two skill levels too high); dsec-21, -22 and -28 are also flagged calc:true although no computation discriminates among the options.
evidence: dsec-21/-22: every numeric option is $8,000 (only the location differs: OCI vs income vs RE), so the item tests only "AFS -> OCI" / "trading -> NI"; they are near-duplicates (Jaccard 0.83) of each other and of remembering-labeled dsec-11. dsec-23: answer is the label "At amortized cost" (recall that HTM is not marked to FV; same fact as dsec-19, labeled application/2, and far-x2-23, labeled remembering/1). dsec-17 and dsec-25: recall of one ASC 320-10-35-10 transfer rule each, no facts to analyze. dsec-28: recall that CECL applies at purchase; the $4,000 is given in the stem. Blueprint definitions: Remembering & Understanding = knowledge of the topic; Analysis = examining interrelationships to identify causes/find evidence (reconstructed tasks use "analyze, reconcile, detect, investigate and correct"). Batch label counts (practice+exam): application 15, analysis 12, remembering 4 -> after relabeling these six, the module has no analysis-level MCQ that actually requires analysis and remembering rises from 13% to ~32%+ of items, so the section skill-mix target (R&U 5-15, App 45-55, Analysis 35-45) is being met on paper only.
source: AICPA 2026 Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill-level definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel dsec-17, -21, -22, -23, -25, -28 as skill "remembering"; difficulty 1 for -21, -22, -23, -28 and 2 for -17, -25; set calc:false on -21, -22, -28. To keep the analysis share, replace two of them (e.g., -21 and -22) with genuine analysis items (e.g., a two-year AFS roll-forward of amortized cost, FVA balance and AOCI with a sale in year 2, or a classification-reconciliation of a mixed portfolio).

issue: Skill labels one level off: one-step calculations labeled analysis (dsec-05, -16, -18, -24, -26, -27) and pure recall items labeled application (dsec-12, -19, -20, far-x2-13).
evidence: dsec-05/-16/-24: realized gain = proceeds - amortized cost (87,000-80,000; 108,000-100,000; 57,000-50,000) - a one-step "calculate realized gains" (Blueprint reconstructed task FAR-II.E.1.3, Application). dsec-18/-27: allowance = min(ECL, AC-FV) = min(20,000, 15,000) / min(5,000, 3,000) - one-step application. dsec-26: 15,000-6,000 = 9,000 OCI - application. dsec-12: intent to sell -> write down through earnings (no facts to apply). dsec-19: amortized cost 98,000 is given; nothing is computed. dsec-20: which category sends UHG to OCI - recall. far-x2-13: AFS non-credit decline -> $0 in NI (calc:false) - recall.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprints skill definitions; review/reference/blueprint-tasks.csv FAR-II.E.1.1-E.1.3
fix: Relabel dsec-05, -16, -18, -24, -26, -27 as application; dsec-12, -19, -20 and far-x2-13 as remembering (difficulty 1-2). Recompute the module skill mix after the change.

issue: Distractor trap labels or rationales do not describe the error that produces the number.
evidence: Reproduced each distractor: dsec-16 (c) $6,000 = only the AOCI gain reclassified, but its rationale says "Use amortized cost" (the error is recognizing only the reclassified portion; using amortized cost is what the KEY does). dsec-18 (b) $5,000 = 20,000 ECL - 15,000 shortfall (the unrecognized excess), labeled "reversed" with rationale "That is the excess" - nothing is reversed. dsec-24 (b) $5,000 = AOCI amount only, labeled "wrong-classification" (it is a partial computation; the same error in dsec-05 (b) is labeled partial-computation). dsec-26 (d) "$6,000 in OCI; $9,000 in income" is a swap, labeled "wrong-sign" (identical swap in far-dsec-chk2 (d) is labeled "reversed"). dsec-05 (c) $13,000 = 7,000 + 6,000 double count, labeled "overgeneralization".
fix: dsec-16 (c): "This recognizes only the $6,000 reclassified from AOCI; the realized gain is 108,000 - 100,000 = 8,000." dsec-18 (b): trap partial-computation, "5,000 is the part of the expected loss that the fair-value floor disallows (20,000 - 15,000)." dsec-24 (b): trap partial-computation. dsec-26 (d): trap reversed. dsec-05 (c): trap other (double counting) with rationale "adds the 6,000 AOCI reclassification on top of the 7,000 realized gain".

issue: Thin explanations: item-level explanations state the rule with no computation, and several distractor rationales are circular ("Not the treatment", "Not the computation", "Not for trading", "Not face value").
evidence: Item explanations with no numbers although the item is calc: dsec-13 ("income = carrying amount x effective rate"), -14 (no 200,000-185,000 = 15,000 credit loss vs 30,000 floor; 30,000-15,000 = 15,000 OCI), -15, -16, -18, -24, -26, -27. Circular distractor rationales: dsec-21 (d) "Not the treatment.", -22 (d) "Not the treatment.", -24 (c) "Not the computation.", -25 (d) "Not the treatment.", -27 (d) "Not the computation." (8,000 = 5,000 ECL + 3,000 shortfall), -17 (d) "Not for trading.", -23 (b) "Not face value." Brief section 2 check 4 requires the item explanation to state the rule and show the computation.
fix: Add the computation to each item explanation (e.g., dsec-14: "Credit loss = 200,000 - 185,000 = 15,000, below the 30,000 fair-value floor -> allowance and earnings 15,000; remaining 30,000 - 15,000 = 15,000 to OCI"; dsec-27: "min(5,000 ECL, 100,000 - 97,000 = 3,000) = 3,000"). Rewrite each circular rationale to name the error (e.g., dsec-24 (c): "57,000 is the total proceeds, not the gain"; dsec-25 (d): "transfers never go directly to retained earnings; HTM -> AFS unrealized gains go to OCI under ASC 320-10-35-10(c)").

issue: Stem "unrealized holding gains bypass net income" is literally true of HTM as well (HTM unrealized gains never reach net income), and the explanation for (c) ("Unrealized gains aren't recognized") confirms that they bypass NI; the intended contrast (recognized, but in OCI) is not stated.
evidence: HTM: fair value changes are not recognized (ASC 320-10-35-1(a)); so they also "bypass net income". The key (a) relies on the reader inferring "are recognized outside net income".
fix: Reword: "For which classification of debt securities are unrealized holding gains recognized, but in other comprehensive income rather than net income?"

issue: Answer cue and unanswerable amount: three options are dollar amounts and the key is the only non-numeric label ("At amortized cost"); the stem gives no coupon, yield or term, so the amortized cost cannot be computed, which is why the key avoids a number.
evidence: Options: $99,000 / $100,000 / "At amortized cost" / "$96,000, unchanged". Format mismatch singles out (c). Same fact is tested in dsec-19 and far-x2-23.
fix: Give coupon and yield (e.g., 8% coupon, 9% yield, bought January 1) and key the computed amortized cost ($96,640), with $99,000 (FV), $96,000 (no amortization) and $95,360 (wrong sign) as distractors - or make every option a non-numeric measurement basis. Consider retiring it as redundant with dsec-19.

evidence: dsec-19 (b) $100,000 "Par isn't used" - face value is never given in the stem, so the number has no source; (c) "$4,000 above cost" is not a reportable amount. dsec-24 (c) $57,000 (the total proceeds reported as the gain). far-x2-13 (c) $190,000 (the fair value itself as a loss) and (d) $5,000 (an arbitrary half of the decline). None of these models a misconception a CPA candidate would plausibly hold.
fix: dsec-19: state face $100,000 in the stem and replace (c) with "$98,000 less a $4,000 valuation allowance" or "$100,000 (face)". dsec-24 (c): $2,000 vs $5,000 already cover partial errors; replace with $12,000 (7,000 + 5,000 double count). x2-13 (c)/(d): use "$10,000 in net income as a credit loss" and "$10,000 reclassified to net income at year-end".

issue: Answer cues: the key alone echoes the stem's technical wording.
evidence: chk2 key "$25,000 credit loss in NI; $35,000 in OCI" and dsec-14 key "$15,000 credit loss in earnings; $15,000 in OCI" are the only options that carry the stem term "credit loss" (the parallel reversed option omits it), and both are much the longest (cues.md). dsec-09 stem asks how "expected credit losses" are recognized and only the key says "expected ... credit losses (CECL)"; distractor (b) carries the only absolute ("Only when").
fix: Make options parallel: e.g., chk2 "(c) $25,000 in net income; $35,000 in OCI" vs "(d) $35,000 in net income; $25,000 in OCI"; dsec-14 drop "credit loss" from the key; dsec-09 change the stem to "How are credit losses on HTM debt securities recognized..." and word the key "Through an allowance measured at lifetime expected losses from initial recognition".

issue: Redundancy: the same three facts are each tested the same way 3-5 times, while multi-step and analysis-level situations are not tested at all.
evidence: Trading UHG -> NI: dsec-04, -11, -22 (+ TBS u7 d4, r3 r4). AFS UHG -> OCI: dsec-20, -21, far-x2-13 (+ pre1, TBS d3, r5). HTM at amortized cost, FV ignored: dsec-19, -23, far-x2-23 (+ TBS d1, r3). AFS sale gain = proceeds - AC with AOCI reclassified: dsec-05, -16, -24 (same template: 80k/87k/6k, 100k/108k/6k, 50k/57k/5k). dsec-21 and -22 are near-identical stems (Jaccard 0.83). Not tested by any MCQ: premium amortization beyond Year 1 / carrying amount after two years, interest income on an AFS security that carries a fair value adjustment, AFS -> HTM transfer, credit-loss recovery (allowance reversal through NI), intent-to-sell write-down with numbers, HTM sale/tainting.
fix: Retire or rewrite dsec-21, -22 (keep -04, -11), dsec-23 (keep -19, x2-23) and one of dsec-16/-24; replace them with items on the untested situations listed, at application/analysis level.

issue: Exam-pool item far-x2-12 reuses practice item dsec-13's bond exactly ($100,000 face, 8% coupon, $96,000 price, 9% yield, HTM), so a candidate who practiced dsec-13 has already computed $8,640 and the mock item measures recall of a seen problem.
evidence: dsec-13 key: 96,000 x 9% = 8,640 interest income. x2-12 key: 96,000 + (8,640 - 8,000) = 96,640 carrying amount - the second step of the same computation on identical numbers.
source: REVIEW.md "Mock forms" (exam-pool items are meant to be new)
fix: Change x2-12's numbers (e.g., $200,000 face, 6% coupon, 7% yield, price $191,800 -> interest 13,426, carrying 193,226) or change dsec-13's.

issue: Stem opens "Using the facts in the previous item", but practice and mixed sets are shuffled (src/lib/quiz.ts shuffle/interleave), so the "previous item" is usually a different question.
evidence: quiz.ts lines 84-135 shuffle and interleave picked items. The parenthetical restates price, coupon, face and yield, so the item is answerable, but the lead-in is confusing and omits the January 1 purchase date and annual December 31 coupon that make "end of Year 1" unambiguous.
fix: Make it standalone: "On January 1, a company bought a $300,000, 5% bond (interest paid annually December 31) for $288,000 to yield 6% and classified it as HTM. What is its amortized cost at December 31?"

issue: Rows r4 (unrealized gain on Bond A in net income) and r5 (unrealized loss on Bond B in OCI) are period amounts, but the exhibit never says when Bonds A and B were acquired or what they were carried at last year; the keys (4,000 and 6,000) assume both were bought during the current year at amortized cost.
evidence: Exhibit gives only December 31 amortized cost and fair value for A and B; only Bond C has a purchase date (January 1). If Bond A was held at the prior year-end at, say, 102,000 FV, the current-year NI gain is 2,000, not 4,000; likewise r5 could be a cumulative AOCI balance or a current-year OCI amount.
fix: Add to the Holdings exhibit: "All three bonds were bought on January 1 of the current year (Bonds A and B at their amortized cost shown)." Optionally relabel r5 "Unrealized loss on Bond B in OCI for the year".

issue: Lesson-item alignment gap: the lesson never teaches HTM eligibility limits or transfers between categories, yet the inline check far-dsec-chk1 and practice items far-dsec-17 and far-dsec-25 test them (and the item explanations are one-liners), so a learner routed back to the lesson after a miss finds nothing.
evidence: Lesson body: HTM row says only "Positive intent and ability to hold to maturity". Not taught: a security that may be sold in response to interest-rate changes or liquidity needs cannot be HTM (ASC 320-10-25-4) - tested by chk1; the four transfer rules of ASC 320-10-35-10 (from trading: no reversal; into trading: earnings immediately - dsec-17; HTM -> AFS: OCI - dsec-25; AFS -> HTM: AOCI amortized over remaining life, offsetting the premium/discount) and that transfers into or out of trading should be rare (ASC 320-10-35-12). No flashcard covers transfers either.
fix: Add a short "Who qualifies for HTM, and transfers" section after the three-bucket table: the 25-4 disqualifiers, a 4-row transfer table (from/to, measurement at transfer, where the unrealized gain/loss goes), and the "tainting" note for sales/transfers out of HTM; add a flashcard on transfers and cite ASC 320-10-35-10.

issue: Credit-loss measurement is not taught: the lesson says only "the credit portion" goes to an allowance, but never says how the credit loss is measured for AFS (amortized cost minus the present value of expected cash flows at the effective rate, then capped at AC - FV) or that later improvements reverse the allowance through net income. far-dsec-14 depends on the PV-of-expected-cash-flows measure.
evidence: dsec-14: AC 200,000, FV 170,000, PV of expected cash flows 185,000 -> credit loss 200,000 - 185,000 = 15,000 (< 30,000 floor) in earnings, 15,000 OCI. The lesson has no sentence that maps "PV of expected cash flows" to the credit loss; the lesson also has no worked numbers for the cap (tested by dsec-18 and -27).
fix: In "Credit losses", add: "AFS credit loss = amortized cost - PV of expected cash flows (discounted at the effective rate), limited to AC - FV; later decreases in expected losses reverse the allowance through net income." Add a 3-line worked example (e.g., AC 200,000; FV 170,000; PV 185,000 -> 15,000 NI / 15,000 OCI) and one cap example (ECL 20,000 > shortfall 15,000 -> allowance 15,000).

issue: Valuation-account mechanics are not taught: the lesson mentions a "fair value adjustment" account in one sentence but never shows that each period's entry is the change from the existing balance to the required balance, nor the sale/reclassification entry, which far-dsec-08 and the far-tbs-u7-debt-securities journal part require.
evidence: dsec-08: required 158,000 - 150,000 = 8,000 Dr less existing 3,000 Dr -> 5,000 entry. TBS u7 JE: required 390,000 - 385,535 = 4,465 Dr; existing 1,005 Cr -> 5,470 Dr. The lesson's only fair-value example is a first-year adjustment with no prior balance (93,376 -> 95,000 = 1,624).
fix: Extend "Fair value adjustments" with a Year 2 roll-forward of the lesson's own bond (amortized cost 94,846; assume FV 94,000 -> required 846 Cr; existing 1,624 Dr -> entry Dr OCI 2,470 / Cr FVA 2,470) as a je block, and add a sale je block showing the realized gain and the AOCI reclassification.

issue: Several bond prices are not the present value of the stated cash flows at the stated yield for any annual (or semiannual) term, so a learner who checks the price cannot reproduce it.
evidence: Python PV checks: lesson faded example $200,000 10% at 9% priced $207,580 - no term matches (5-yr annual 207,779; semiannual 5-yr 207,913). dsec-02/-03 $300,000 5% at 6% priced $288,000 - between 4-yr 289,605 and 5-yr 287,363. far-x2-12 (five-year, 8% at 9%) priced $96,000 vs PV 96,110 (dsec-13 uses the same bond; implied yield about 9.03%). TBS r3 Bond C $150,000 5% at 6% priced $146,830 - between 2-yr 147,250 and 3-yr 145,990. By contrast the lesson worked example (92,015), dsec-10 (105,154) and TBS u7 (372,902) are exact. Keys are unaffected because each item gives the price.
source: Arithmetic (PV of annuity + PV of face)
fix: Either state a term and use the exact PV (e.g., faded example 5-year price 207,779 -> interest 18,700, amortization 1,300, AC 206,479, OCI loss 3,479; x2-12/dsec-13 $96,110) or add "(price given; ignore the term)" so careful learners are not confused.

issue: Frontmatter: objective 3 has no Blueprint task mapping and is labeled "analysis" although recording fair value changes, credit losses and sales is a "prepare journal entries" application task; citations omit the ASC 320-10 paragraphs the items rely on.
evidence: objectives[2]: skill analysis, no task. Reconstructed task FAR-II.E.1.2 "Prepare journal entries for changes in fair value ... including reclassification adjustments" is Application. Citations list 320-10, 326-20/-30 and 310-20-35 only.
fix: Set objective 3 skill to application with task "Prepare journal entries for changes in fair value of debt securities, including reclassification adjustments"; add citations ASC 320-10-35-4 (interest income incl. amortization for all categories) and 320-10-35-10 (transfers).

issue: fc1 packs three classifications into one card (not atomic); fc6 packs two rules and omits the "more likely than not required to sell" trigger.
evidence: fc1 back: HTM / Trading / AFS measurement and UHG location in one answer. fc6 back: "Intent to sell -> write down to FV through NI" - ASC 326-30-35-10 also triggers the write-down when it is more likely than not the entity will be required to sell before recovery (the lesson states this; the card does not).
fix: Split fc1 into three cards (one per category) or keep it as a summary but add per-category cards; split fc6 into "AFS credit-loss allowance cap" and "Intent to sell (or MLTN required to sell) before recovery -> write down AC to FV through NI".
